text: We identified a non-conformance during the inspection of Fuselage frame bracket part number FR-42352-C, supplied by PrecisionFlow Systems, on June 3, 2022. Inspection revealed a coating adhesion failure, which was classified as a minor defect. The affected area exhibited a lack of cohesion between the coating and the substrate, indicating a failure of the coating to properly adhere to the part. We determined that the root cause of the defect was a process parameter drift, specifically a deviation in oven temperature control during the coating application process. Further investigation revealed that the oven temperature had fluctuated beyond the specified tolerance, resulting in an inadequate coating cure. This fluctuation was not detected in real-time, allowing the defective part to proceed through the production process. We acknowledged that the defect, although minor, could potentially impact the structural integrity of the fuselage frame bracket if not addressed. Consequently, we decided to rework the part in-house to ensure compliance with the required specifications. The rework process will involve stripping and reapplying the coating, followed by a thorough inspection to verify the defect has been successfully corrected. To prevent similar defects from occurring in the future, we will review and update the training records for the operators involved in the coating process. This corrective action will ensure that all personnel understand the importance of maintaining precise process control, particularly with regards to oven temperature, and are aware of the procedures for detecting and responding to process deviations. By taking these measures, we aim to prevent recurrence of this defect and maintain the high quality standards expected in our aerospace manufacturing operations.

root_cause: Drawing revision not communicated to production floor
corrective_action: Supplier to submit updated PPAP within 30 days
text: We identified a critical non-conformance in the avionics bay panel, part number AV-36940-F, supplied by Vanguard Coatings Inc, during a routine inspection on February 15, 2023. Inspection revealed porosity in the coating, which was detected through X-ray examination. The presence of porosity is a significant concern as it can compromise the structural integrity and environmental sealing of the avionics bay, potentially leading to system failures and safety risks. Further investigation into the cause of the non-conformance revealed that the issue stemmed from a revision to the drawing that was not effectively communicated to the production floor. This oversight resulted in the application of an outdated process, leading to the porosity defects observed in the finished parts. We consider this defect to be critical due to its potential impact on the overall performance and reliability of the aircraft systems. In light of this finding, we have determined that the affected parts will be returned to the supplier, Vanguard Coatings Inc, for rectification. As part of the corrective action, we require the supplier to submit an updated Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) package within 30 days, which will include revised process controls and inspection procedures to prevent similar defects from occurring in future productions. This updated PPAP will be reviewed and approved by our quality team to ensure that all necessary measures are in place to prevent recurrence of this critical non-conformance.

root_cause: Measurement system error — gauge R&R not current
corrective_action: 100% incoming inspection implemented until supplier corrective action verified
text: We identified a non-conformance in the Hydraulic Actuator Assembly, Part Number AS-30218-B, supplied by Helix Tooling Solutions, during our routine inspection process on May 23, 2024. Inspection revealed a thread form deviation that did not meet the specified requirements. Although the defect was deemed minor in terms of its impact on the overall functionality of the assembly, it still fell outside of our acceptable limits, prompting further investigation into the root cause. Our analysis indicated that the root cause of the non-conformance was attributed to a measurement system error on the part of the supplier. Specifically, it was discovered that the gauge used for measuring the thread form had not undergone the required recalibration and gauge R&R (repeatability and reproducibility) study, leading to inaccurate measurements. This oversight resulted in parts being shipped that did not meet our specifications. Given the nature of the defect and its root cause, we determined that the appropriate disposition for the non-conforming parts was Return to Supplier (RTS). This decision ensures that Helix Tooling Solutions can rectify their measurement system issues and prevent future occurrences of this non-conformance. In addition to returning the affected parts, we have also implemented a corrective action to conduct 100% incoming inspection on all shipments of Part Number AS-30218-B from this supplier until such time as their corrective actions have been verified and validated. This enhanced inspection protocol will provide an additional layer of quality control, safeguarding against the acceptance of non-conforming parts and ensuring compliance with our stringent quality standards.

text: We identified a non-conformance in the FR-24440-C fuselage frame bracket, supplied by Titan Alloy Works, during a routine X-ray inspection on May 19, 2024. Inspection revealed the presence of porosity in the bracket, which is a defect that can potentially compromise the structural integrity of the part. We classified the defect as minor, as it does not pose an immediate risk to the safety of the aircraft, but it still requires attention to prevent any potential issues during subsequent assembly and operation. Our investigation into the root cause of the defect revealed that the porosity was likely caused by an environmental control failure in the supplier's clean room. Specifically, we found that the humidity levels in the clean room exceeded the acceptable limits, leading to the formation of porosity in the part. We notified the supplier of the issue and worked with them to implement corrective actions to prevent similar defects in the future. We accepted the defective part conditionally, with the stipulation that it will be reinspected at the next assembly stage to ensure that it does not pose any risk to the overall quality of the aircraft. In the meantime, we have implemented 100% incoming inspection for all parts received from Titan Alloy Works until we can verify that the supplier has implemented effective corrective actions to prevent similar defects. This additional inspection will provide an extra layer of quality control, ensuring that any defective parts are detected and addressed before they can enter the production stream.

root_cause: Measurement system error — gauge R&R not current
corrective_action: Supplier quality engineer site visit scheduled
text: We identified a non-conformance with the AV-77404-F avionics bay panel supplied by CoreTech Forgings during our incoming inspection on February 19, 2022. Inspection revealed that the part exceeded the maximum allowable dimensional tolerance for several critical features, rendering it unacceptable for use in our aircraft assembly. The severity of this defect is deemed critical, as it directly impacts the structural integrity and safety of the avionics bay. Further investigation into the cause of the non-conformance revealed that the measurement system used by CoreTech Forgings was not properly calibrated, and their gauge repeatability and reproducibility (R&R) study was not current. This lack of attention to measurement system validation led to inaccurate measurements, resulting in parts being shipped outside of specified tolerances. We consider this root cause to be a significant concern, as it suggests a potential lack of control over their manufacturing process. Given the critical nature of this defect and the fact that it can be corrected without scrapping the part, we have decided to rework the affected panels in-house to bring them into specification. This will ensure that the parts meet our stringent quality standards and are safe for use in our aircraft. To prevent similar issues from arising in the future, we have scheduled a site visit with CoreTech Forgings' quality engineer to review their measurement system and gauge calibration procedures, and to provide guidance on how to improve their processes to prevent such errors. This corrective action will help to ensure that parts supplied by CoreTech Forgings meet our requirements and are free from defects.

root_cause: Measurement system error — gauge R&R not current
corrective_action: Supplier quality engineer site visit scheduled
text: We identified a non-conformance with part number AV-63655-F, an avionics bay panel supplied by Apex Precision Components, during our routine inspection process on June 7, 2024. Inspection revealed that the torque specification for the panel's fasteners had been exceeded, which is a major defect due to the potential impact on the structural integrity and safety of the aircraft. Our initial review of the supplier's documentation indicated that the torque values had been recorded within the acceptable range, but our independent verification revealed otherwise. Further investigation into the cause of the non-conformance revealed a measurement system error, specifically that the gauge used for torque measurement had not undergone regular recalibration as required. As a result, the measurements taken by the supplier were inaccurate, leading to the over-torquing of the fasteners. We consider this a major defect, as it could compromise the performance and reliability of the avionics system. Given the severity of the defect and the fact that it cannot be reworked, we have determined that the affected parts must be scrapped to prevent any potential risk. We have notified the supplier of the non-conformance and have scheduled a site visit by our quality engineer to work with their team to address the root cause. The purpose of this visit is to ensure that the supplier's quality control processes, including their measurement system, are brought up to date and that corrective actions are implemented to prevent similar defects from occurring in the future. We will continue to monitor the supplier's performance and implement additional controls as necessary to ensure the quality of the parts supplied to us.

root_cause: Worn tooling — CNC lathe axis calibration drift
disposition: Conditional acceptance — reinspection at next assembly
corrective_action: 100% incoming inspection implemented until supplier corrective action verified
text: We identified a non-conformance with the Fuel line coupling, part number FU-55646-G, supplied by Atlas Machining Group, during our routine inspection process on 2024-03-30. Inspection revealed a coating adhesion failure, which is classified as a major defect due to its potential impact on the overall performance and safety of the aerospace system. The coating is a critical feature of the fuel line coupling, providing corrosion resistance and ensuring a reliable seal. Further investigation into the root cause of the defect revealed that the issue is attributed to worn tooling, specifically a CNC lathe axis calibration drift. This drift resulted in inconsistent machining operations, leading to a compromised coating adhesion. We worked closely with the supplier to understand the extent of the issue and to develop a corrective action plan. As an interim measure, we have implemented a 100% incoming inspection for all fuel line couplings received from Atlas Machining Group until such time that their corrective actions are verified and validated. We have conditionally accepted the affected parts, with the understanding that they will undergo reinspection at the next assembly stage. This conditional acceptance is based on the risk assessment and the implementation of additional inspection controls to ensure that the defect does not propagate to the final product. We will continue to monitor the situation closely and work with the supplier to ensure that the root cause is fully addressed and that the corrective actions are effective in preventing future occurrences of this defect.

root_cause: Environmental control failure — humidity exceedance in clean room
corrective_action: Process FMEA to be updated with new failure mode
text: We identified a critical non-conformance during the inspection of part number CS-64151-H, a control surface hinge supplied by CoreTech Forgings, on November 18, 2024. Inspection revealed a thread form deviation that exceeded the acceptable limits specified in the engineering drawing. The defect was detected during a routine dimensional inspection, where we measured the thread pitch and major diameter of the hinge pin hole. Our measurements indicated that the thread form did not conform to the required specifications, rendering the part unusable for its intended application. Further investigation into the cause of the non-conformance revealed that the defect was likely due to an environmental control failure in the supplier's clean room. It was determined that the humidity level in the clean room had exceeded the specified limits, resulting in an adverse effect on the machining process. This excess humidity led to a degradation of the cutting tool's performance, ultimately causing the thread form deviation. We consider this defect to be critical, as it affects the structural integrity and reliability of the control surface hinge, which is a safety-critical component. As a result of this non-conformance, we have decided to return the affected parts to the supplier, CoreTech Forgings, for correction or replacement. In addition, we will update our process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) to include this new failure mode, ensuring that we take proactive measures to prevent similar defects from occurring in the future. We will also work closely with the supplier to implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence, including improvements to their environmental control systems and machining processes.

root_cause: Operator error — incorrect fixture setup
corrective_action: 100% incoming inspection implemented until supplier corrective action verified
text: We identified a non-conformance with Part Number PN-92974-A, a turbine blade used in stage 2 of our engine assembly, which was supplied by NovaTech Composites. The issue was discovered on April 11, 2025, during our routine inspection process. Inspection revealed that the surface finish of the turbine blade did not meet the required specifications, indicating a major defect. This non-conformance is classified as major due to the critical nature of the part's function and the potential impact on engine performance and safety. Further investigation into the cause of the non-conformance revealed that operator error at the supplier's facility was the root cause. It was determined that an incorrect fixture setup was used during the manufacturing process, leading to the unacceptable surface finish. We consider this a significant issue because the surface finish of turbine blades is crucial for maintaining optimal engine efficiency and preventing potential failures. Given the severity of the defect and its potential consequences, we have determined that the affected parts must be scrapped to ensure the quality and reliability of our final product. To prevent similar issues in the future, we are implementing a 100% incoming inspection for all turbine blades received from NovaTech Composites until we can verify that the supplier has taken corrective action to address the root cause. This additional inspection step will provide an extra layer of quality control, enabling us to detect and reject any non-conforming parts before they are integrated into our engine assemblies. We will continue to work closely with NovaTech Composites to ensure that their corrective actions are effective and sustainable, ultimately enhancing the overall quality of their supplied components.

root_cause: Process parameter drift — oven temperature control
disposition: Use As Is (UAI) — Engineering disposition required
corrective_action: Supplier quality engineer site visit scheduled
text: We identified a non-conformance during the inspection of part number FR-33108-C, a fuselage frame bracket supplied by NovaTech Composites, on November 29, 2023. Inspection revealed a burr on the critical datum surface of the component, which is a major defect that affects the part's fit and function. The burr, measuring 0.05 mm in height, was detected using a precision profilometer and verified through visual inspection. We determined that the defect is a result of process parameter drift, specifically related to oven temperature control during the manufacturing process. Further analysis indicated that the supplier's oven temperature control system had deviated from the specified parameters, leading to an inconsistent curing process. This inconsistency caused the formation of the burr on the critical datum surface. We classified the severity of this non-conformance as major due to its potential impact on the structural integrity and safety of the aircraft. As a result, we require an engineering disposition to determine the suitability of the affected parts for use. We have designated the disposition as Use As Is (UAI), pending further evaluation and approval from our engineering team. To address the root cause of this non-conformance, we have scheduled a site visit with NovaTech Composites' quality engineer to review their manufacturing process and implement corrective actions. The focus of this visit will be to assess and adjust their oven temperature control system to prevent similar defects from occurring in the future. We will work closely with the supplier to ensure that their processes are brought back under control and that all parts meet our stringent quality standards.

root_cause: Operator error — incorrect fixture setup
corrective_action: Supplier to submit updated PPAP within 30 days
text: We identified a non-conformance in the LG-57703-D landing gear strut fitting, supplied by Orbital Fasteners Ltd, during our incoming inspection process on 2025-03-13. Inspection revealed a thread form deviation that exceeded the acceptable limits defined in the engineering drawing. The defect was classified as major due to its potential impact on the structural integrity and safety of the landing gear assembly. We immediately notified the supplier and initiated an investigation to determine the root cause of the non-conformance. Our analysis indicated that the thread form deviation was caused by operator error at the supplier's facility, resulting from an incorrect setup of the machining fixture. This error led to an inconsistent thread profile, which was not detected during the supplier's quality control process. We worked closely with the supplier to verify the root cause and develop a plan to address the issue. As a result, we decided to rework the affected parts in-house to ensure compliance with the engineering requirements. To prevent similar non-conformances in the future, we required the supplier to submit an updated Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) package within 30 days, which will include revised procedures for fixture setup and inspection. We will review and approve the updated PPAP to ensure that it meets our quality standards. Additionally, we will continue to monitor the supplier's performance and conduct regular audits to verify implementation of the corrective actions. By taking these steps, we aim to prevent recurrence of this defect and maintain the high level of quality expected in our aerospace components.
